exampleAnswers.title: Calculating a Minor in a 3x3 Matrix With Integer Entries

question.text:
For the matrix
$
    {Y} = 
    \left\lbrack
    \matrix {
        7 & -4 & 2 \\
        1 & 3 & 5 \\
        0 & -2 & 6
    }
    \right\rbrack,
$
find the minor $M_{13}$ of the entry $y_{13}.$
question.explanation:
The minor of $y_{13} = 2$ (first row, third column) is the determinant of the remaining entries when the column and row containing $2$ are removed:

\[ {Y} = \left\lbrack \matrix { \color{gray}{\ast} & \color{gray}{\ast} & \bbox[lightgray, 2pt]{\color{gray}2} \\ 1 & 3 & \color{gray}{\ast} \\ 0 & -2 & \color{gray}{\ast} } \right\rbrack \]

So, the minor of $y_{13}=2$ is

\begin{align*} M_{13} &= \text{det} \left[ \begin{array}{cc} 1 & 3 \\ 0 & -2 \end{array} \right] \\[5pt] &= \left| \begin{array}{cc} 1 & 3 \\ 0 & -2 \end{array} \right| \\[5pt] &= 1 \cdot (-2) - 3 \cdot 0 \\[5pt] &= -2 - 0 \\[5pt] &= \bbox[4pt,border: 1px solid gainsboro]{ -2 }. \end{align*}

question.text: Calculate the minor of the entry $d_{23}$ in the matrix $ {D} = \left\lbrack \matrix { 10 & 2 & 5 \\ -12 & 44 & -33 \\ 25 & 30 & 41 } \right\rbrack. $
question.explanation:
The minor of $d_{23} = -33$ (second row, third column) is the determinant of the remaining entries when the column and row containing $-33$ are removed:

\[ {D} = \left\lbrack \matrix { 10 & 2 & {\color{gray}\ast} \\ {\color{gray}\ast} & {\color{gray}\ast} & \bbox[lightgray, 2pt]{\color{gray}-33} \\ 25 & 30 & {\color{gray}\ast} } \right\rbrack \]

So, the minor of $d_{23}=-33$ is

\begin{align*} \text{det} \left[ \begin{array}{cc} 10 & 2 \\ 25 & 30 \end{array} \right] &= \left| \begin{array}{cc} 10 & 2 \\ 25 & 30 \end{array} \right| \\[5pt] &= 10 \cdot 30 - 2 \cdot 25 \\[5pt] &= 300-50 \\[5pt] &= 250. \end{align*}

question.text:
For the matrix
$
    {P} = 
    \left\lbrack
    \matrix {
        5 & -2 & 1 \\
        0 & 3 & 4 \\
        6 & 2 & -1
    }
    \right\rbrack.
$
find the minor $M_{12}$ of the entry $p_{12}.$
question.explanation:
The minor of $p_{12} = -2$ (first row, second column) is the determinant of the remaining entries when the column and row containing $-2$ are removed:

\[ {P} = \left\lbrack \matrix { \color{gray}{\ast} & \bbox[lightgray, 2pt]{\color{gray}{-2}} & \color{gray}{\ast} \\ 0 & \color{gray}{\ast} & 4 \\ 6 & \color{gray}{\ast} & -1 } \right\rbrack \]

So, the minor of $p_{12}=1$ is

\begin{align*} M_{12} &= \text{det} \left[ \begin{array}{cc} 0 & 4 \\ 6 & -1 \end{array} \right] \\[5pt] &= \left| \begin{array}{cc} 0 & 4 \\ 6 & -1 \end{array} \right| \\[5pt] &= 0\cdot (-1) - 4\cdot 6 \\[5pt] &= 0 - 24 \\[5pt] &= \bbox[4pt,border: 1px solid gainsboro]{ -24 }. \end{align*}

example.title: Calculating a Minor in a 3x3 Matrix With Integer Entries

question.text:
For the matrix
$
    {A} = 
    \left\lbrack
    \matrix {
        2 & -4 & 3 \\
        5 & 1 & -1 \\
        0 & 6 & 2
    }
    \right\rbrack.
$
find the minor $M_{23}$ of the entry $a_{23}.$
question.explanation:
The minor of $a_{23} = -1$ (second row, third column) is the determinant of the remaining entries when the column and row containing $-1$ are removed:

\[ {A} = \left\lbrack \matrix { 2 & -4 & {\color{gray}\ast} \\ {\color{gray}\ast} & {\color{gray}\ast} & \bbox[lightgray, 2pt]{\color{gray}{-1}} \\ 0 & 6 & {\color{gray}\ast} } \right\rbrack \]

So, the minor of $a_{23}=-1$ is

\begin{align*} M_{23} &= \text{det} \left[ \begin{array}{cc} 2 & -4 \\ 0 & 6 \end{array} \right] \\[5pt] &= \left| \begin{array}{cc} 2 & -4 \\ 0 & 6 \end{array} \right| \\[5pt] &= 2 \cdot 6 - (-4) \cdot 0 \\[5pt] &= 12 - 0 \\[5pt] &= \bbox[4pt,border: 1px solid gainsboro]{ 12 }. \end{align*}

exampleAnswers.title: Calculating a Minor in a 3x3 Matrix With Variable Entries

question.text: What is the minor of $u_{21}$ in the matrix $ {U} = \left\lbrack \matrix { -4 & j &k-2j \\ kj & j & k \\ 7 & -k & j } \right\rbrack ? $
question.explanation:
First, we remove the second row and the first column:

\[ {U} = \left\lbrack \matrix { {\color{gray}\ast} & j &k-2j \\ {\bbox[lightgray, 2pt]{\color{gray}kj}} & {\color{gray}\ast} & {\color{gray}\ast} \\ \color{gray}\ast & -k & j} \right\rbrack \]

Next, we calculate the determinant:

\begin{align*} \require{cancel} \text{det} \left[ \begin{array}{cc} j & k-2j \\ - k & j \end{array} \right] &= \left|\begin{array}{cc} j& k-2j \\ -k & j \end{array}\right| \\[5pt] &= j \cdot j- ( -k)\cdot (k-2j)\\[5pt] &= j^2+k(k-2j ) \\[5pt] &= j^2+k^2 -k2j \\[5pt] &= j^2-2jk + k^2\\[5pt] &= (j-k)^2 \end{align*}

question.text: What is the minor of $t_{33}$ in the matrix $ {T} = \left\lbrack \matrix { y-x & x & y^2 \\ -x & y+x & 1 \\ x^2 & y^2 & x^2 } \right\rbrack? $
question.explanation:
First, we remove the third row and third column:

\[ {T} = \left\lbrack \matrix { y-x & x & {\color{gray}\ast} \\ -x & y+x & {\color{gray}\ast} \\ {\color{gray}\ast} & {\color{gray}\ast} & \bbox[lightgray, 2pt]{\color{gray}x^2} \\ } \right\rbrack \]

Next, we calculate the determinant:

\begin{align*} \require{cancel} \det \left[ \begin{array}{cc} y-x & x \\ -x & y+x \\ \end{array} \right] &= \left|\begin{array}{cc} y-x & x \\ -x & y+x \\ \end{array}\right| \\[5pt] &= (y-x) \cdot (y+x) - x \cdot (-x) \\[5pt] &= y^2 - x^2+x^2\\[5pt] &= y^2 -\cancel{ x^2}+\cancel{x^2}\\[5pt] &= y^2 \end{align*}

exampleAnswers.title: Solving for an Unknown Given the Value of a Minor

question.text: Given that the minor of $p_{11}$ is $4$, find all the possible values of $t$ in the matrix \[ P=\left[\begin{array}{ccc} -5t & 18 & 6t\\ -3 & 9 & 5\\ 19t &1 & 3t \end{array}\right]. \]
question.explanation:
First, we remove the first row and first column:

\[ P= \left[\begin{array}{ccc} \bbox[lightgray, 2pt]{\color{gray}5t} & {\color{gray}\ast} & {\color{gray}\ast} \\ {\color{gray}\ast} & 9 & 5 \\ {\color{gray}\ast} & 1 & 3t \end{array}\right] \]

The minor of $p_{11}$ is

\begin{align*} \textrm{det}\left[\begin{array}{cc} 9 & 5\\ 1 & 3t \end{array} \right] &= \left|\begin{array}{cc} 9 & 5\\ 1 & 3t \end{array}\right|\\[5pt] &= 9\cdot 3t - 5 \cdot 1 \\[5pt] &=27t-5. \end{align*}

We're told that the minor of $p_{11}$ is $4$, so we must have:

\begin{align*} 27t-5 &=4\\[3pt] 27t &= 9 \\[3pt] %t &= \dfrac{9}{27} \\[3pt] t &= \dfrac{1}{3} \end{align*}

Therefore, the solution is $t=\dfrac{1}{3}.$

question.text: Given that the minor of $d_{31}$ is $43$, find all the possible values of $x$ in the matrix \[ D =\left[\begin{array}{ccc} 8 & 1&-5\\ 9 & 11& x\\ 7 &-5 &3 \end{array}\right]. \]
question.explanation:
First, we remove the third row and first column:

\[ D= \left[\begin{array}{ccc} {\color{gray}\ast} & 1 & -5 \\ {\color{gray}\ast} & 11 & x \\ \bbox[lightgray, 2pt]{\color{gray}7} & {\color{gray}\ast} & {\color{gray}\ast} \end{array}\right] \]

The minor of $d_{31}$ is

\begin{align*} \textrm{det}\left[\begin{array}{cc} 1 & -5\\ 11 &x \end{array} \right] &= \left|\begin{array}{cc} 1 & -5\\ 11 &x \end{array}\right|\\[5pt] &= 1\cdot x - 11\cdot (-5) \\[5pt] &=x+55. \end{align*}

We're told that the minor of $d_{31}$ is $43$, so we must have:

\begin{align*} x+55 &=43 \\[3pt] x&=-12 \end{align*}

Therefore, the solution is $x=-12.$

question.text: Given that the minor of $d_{12}$ is $-4$, find all the possible values of $p$ in the matrix \[ D=\left[\begin{array}{ccc} p^2 & p^3 & 6\\ -6 & 7 & 5\\ 5 & 2+p & p-1 \end{array}\right]. \]
question.explanation:
First, we remove the first row and second column:

\[ D= \left[\begin{array}{ccc} {\color{gray}\ast} & \bbox[lightgray, 2pt]{\color{gray}p^3} & {\color{gray}\ast} \\ -6 & {\color{gray}\ast} & 5 \\ 5 & {\color{gray}\ast} & p-1 \end{array}\right] \]

The minor of $d_{12}$ is

\begin{align*} \textrm{det}\left[\begin{array}{cc} -6 & 5\\ 5 & p-1 \end{array} \right] &= \left|\begin{array}{cc} -6 & 5\\ 5 & p-1 \end{array}\right|\\[5pt] &= -6\cdot (p-1) - 5 \cdot 5\\[5pt] &=-6p-19. \end{align*}

We're told that the minor of $d_{12}$ is $-4$, so we must have:

\begin{align*} -6p-19 &=-4\\[3pt] -6p &= 15 \\[3pt] %p &= -\dfrac{15}{6} \\[3pt] p &= -\dfrac{5}{2} \end{align*}

Therefore, the solution is $p=-\dfrac{5}{2}.$

question.text: Given that the minor of $m_{21}$ is $11$, find all the possible values of $y$ in the matrix \[ M=\left[\begin{array}{ccc} y & \dfrac{3}{2} & y\\ 25 & 4-y & 12y\\ y & 2 & -6y \end{array}\right]. \]
question.explanation:
First, we remove the second row and first column:

\[ M= \left[\begin{array}{ccc} {\color{gray}\ast} & \dfrac{3}{2} & y \\ \bbox[lightgray, 2pt]{\color{gray} 25}& {\color{gray}\ast} & {\color{gray}\ast}\\ {\color{gray}\ast} & 2 & -6y \end{array}\right] \]

The minor of $m_{21}$ is

\begin{align*} \textrm{det}\left[\begin{array}{cc} \dfrac{3}{2} & y\\ 2 & -6y \end{array} \right] &= \left|\begin{array}{cc} \dfrac{3}{2} & y\\ 2 & -6y \end{array}\right|\\[5pt] &= \dfrac{3}{2}\cdot (-6y) - y \cdot 2\\[5pt] &=-11y. \end{align*}

We're told that the minor of $m_{21}$ is $11$, so we must have:

\begin{align*} -11y &=11\\[3pt] %-2y &= -1 \\[3pt] %y &= \dfrac{1}{2} \\[3pt] y &= -1 \end{align*}

Therefore, the solution is $y=-1.$
